transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m running on empty no matter how much I rest. I just don’t have the energy to keep up with anything anymore, and it's getting harder and harder to just get through the day.
Along with the exhaustion, have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, and did this start after a particular stressful event or major life change?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my woodshop and fishing, and I hardly even touch my gear anymore. It all started shortly after my employer announced a restructuring and I had to start facing the prospect of retirement. Ever since then, this heavy, empty feeling has just taken over and I can't seem to shake it.

Before this started around the job restructuring and retirement stress, have you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things? If so, did it happen at a different time in your life?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I’ve ever felt this kind of heavy depression and lost interest in everything.

Since this started after the restructuring and retirement news, do your feelings seem mainly tied to that stress and ease when you’re distracted from it, or are you feeling depressed and unable to enjoy anything most of the day no matter what’s going on?

No, it doesn't ease up at all, and this dark, drained mood has pretty much become my constant baseline. It doesn't lift even if I try to distract myself, and on weekends when I have free time, I just sit there feeling empty. I can't even bring myself to enjoy woodworking or fishing anymore, no matter what is going on around me.

Since this began, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? If so, which of these have you been experiencing?

Yes, I've been struggling with several of those things; my appetite has completely dropped off to where my pants are loose, and I can't shake this heavy guilt that I've failed my family by only ever being a janitor. It's gotten so dark that I often lie in bed wishing I wouldn't wake up, sometimes picturing driving my car off the highway or taking all my blood pressure pills, though I haven't actually set up a plan to do it. It just feels like my whole life has been a waste and I'm too tired to care anymore.

When you feel this guilty and hopeless, have you ever heard voices others couldn’t hear or become convinced of things like having ruined your family or being beyond help, even when others said that wasn’t true?

Yes, especially at night when I'm alone in the house, I often hear a low male voice whispering my name and calling me a failure. I also can't shake the feeling that I've completely failed my family by never doing anything bigger than cleaning buildings, and I just replay all my mistakes over and over in my head.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime major depressive episode with pervasive depressed mood/anhedonia, neurovegetative symptoms, excessive guilt/worthlessness, and recurrent suicidal ideation, accompanied by mood-congruent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusional guilt/failure). Symptoms are not limited to transient stress-linked distress and persist most of the day. This supports severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
